# Outcome sub-dossier — Sensata Technologies Holding plc (successor entity) realized record, ~2020-2022 (3-5 years after the 2018 closing)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`

> how the closing-time transaction was structured.

## Public-reporting continuity after closing
- Following the February 2018 closing, the registrant continued filing under the same
  SEC filer (CIK 1477294), now as "Sensata Technologies Holding plc," including a Form
  10-K for fiscal year 2022 filed February 13, 2023, covering the years ended December
  31, 2022, 2021, and 2020. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022]
- That Form 10-K was signed by Jeff Cote as Chief Executive Officer and President, and by
  Paul Vasington as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022]
- The fixed outcome window used here is fiscal years 2020-2022, drawn from this single
  Form 10-K's reported and comparative figures (approximately 2-5 years after the
  February 2018 closing). [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022]

## Realized financial trajectory (2020-2022)
- Consolidated net revenue: $3,045,578 thousand (FY2020); $3,820,806 thousand (FY2021);
  $4,029,262 thousand (FY2022). [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022, Consolidated Statements of Operations]
- Net income: $164.3 million, 5.4% of net revenue (FY2020); $363.6 million, 9.5% of net
  revenue (FY2021); $310.7 million, 7.7% of net revenue (FY2022) — net income declined
  year-over-year in FY2022 even as net revenue continued to grow. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022, MD&A results table]
- Restructuring and other charges, net: $33.094 million expense (FY2020); $14.942 million
  expense (FY2021); a net gain of $66.700 million (FY2022), the FY2022 figure driven
  substantially by the divestiture of the company's semiconductor test and thermal
  business ("the Qinex Business"). [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022, Note on Restructuring and Other Charges]

## Workforce (point-in-time, end of window)
- As of December 31, 2022 the company reported approximately 20,800 employees
  (approximately 1,700 U.S.-based, approximately 11,600 female, approximately 200 covered
  by collective bargaining) plus approximately 2,200 contract workers. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022, Human Capital Resources]

## Items not found / not applicable in this filing
- The FY2022 Form 10-K contains no discussion of the 2018 cross-border merger or
  reincorporation as an ongoing matter (e.g., no reference to integration issues, tax-rate
  effects, or governance changes specifically tied to that transaction); the filing's
  business description, risk factors, and MD&A address the company's ordinary ongoing
  operations rather than any residual effect of the 2018 change of incorporation. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022]
- No reputable press report specifically tying post-2018 financial or operational
  developments to the 2018 reincorporation (as opposed to ordinary business conditions)
  was located; any such causal claim would be [UNVERIFIED].

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The registrant continued uninterrupted public reporting under the same CIK after the
  2018 closing. Over fiscal years 2020-2022 it reported continued net-revenue growth
  ($3.05B to $4.03B) alongside a net-income trajectory that rose from FY2020 to FY2021 and
  then declined in FY2022 despite further revenue growth, a swing in restructuring/other
  charges from a net expense in 2020-2021 to a net gain in 2022 (substantially reflecting
  a business divestiture unrelated to the 2018 transaction), and a reported year-end 2022
  workforce of approximately 20,800 employees. The filing does not attribute any of these
  developments to the 2018 reincorporation. [SRC: SEC accession 0001477294-23-000010, Form 10-K FY2022]

[SLICE END]
